sentences: In the middle of a canvas that is almost entirely yellow, a vase of sunflowers looks straight back at us.
This is Vincent van Gogh's Sunflowers of 1888, a picture that says so much with one colour.
In August 1888, in the Yellow House at Arles in the south of France, Van Gogh painted sunflowers to decorate the room where his fellow painter Gauguin would soon stay.
He dreamed of a shared studio of the south.
He painted four sunflower canvases in about a week, and this is the fourth of them.
In a letter he wrote that he was painting with the gusto of a Marseillais eating bouillabaisse.
Look at the big flower heads at the top.
These have dropped their petals and gone to seed.
Van Gogh does not hide this fading stage; he paints it head-on, just as boldly as the fresh blooms.
The vase holds fifteen blooms covering a whole life cycle.
The museum counts one bud, seven flowers in full glow, and seven heads beginning to go to seed, so birth, flowering and decline share one vase.
The flower at the centre is in full bloom, showing its orange heart.
Each pointed petal is a single stroke of the brush, so the whole flower seems to push outward with energy in every direction.
The flower heads are built up in paint so thick they seem to rise off the canvas.
In this impasto, the seed heads become small raised dabs of paint, one after another, that feel rough and bristling.
Now, at the lower right, drooping flowers let their withered petals hang down.
Some see in these sunflowers friendship and devotion, and also the old Dutch theme of how brief and fragile life is.
Now look down at the vase.
On it he signed simply "Vincent" in blue.
People found his surname hard to pronounce, so he usually signed his pictures with his first name alone.
Background, table and vase are nearly all yellow, and Van Gogh himself called it a picture all in yellow.
Only a thin blue line, where the table meets the wall, divides one yellow from another.
Gauguin arrived on 23 October, and this painting hung in the guest room where he stayed.
That December the two artists quarrelled badly, and their life together ended after just two months.
The painting came to London in 1924, and today it hangs in the National Gallery for everyone to see.
Among the open flowers and the fading ones, which one does your eye rest on first?
